column2: On the authority of Abū Muḥammad al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, the grandson of the Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace) and his sweet basil (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said:
I memorised from the Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace): “Leave what gives you doubt for what does not give you doubt.” Reported by al-Tirmidhī and al-Nasāʾī.
Al-Tirmidhī said: A ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.
“The grandson (sibṭ) of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ”: the son of his daughter Fāṭimah (may Allah be pleased with her).
Wa-rayḥānatuhu (“and his sweet basil”): he likened him, because of his joy and delight in him and his fondness for him, to fragrant basil, which the soul welcomes and finds comfort in.

Mā yurībuka (“what gives you doubt”): with the yāʾ of the present tense carrying fatḥah or ḍammah (yarībuka / yurībuka), fatḥah being more eloquent and better known; that is, what you are uncertain about.
“For what does not give you doubt”: what you are not uncertain about.
A Muslim should build his affairs on certainty,
and be clear-sighted in his religion.

The prohibition of falling into doubtful matters. The hadith is a great foundation of scrupulousness (waraʿ). Al-Tirmidhī reported from the hadith of ʿAṭiyyah al-Saʿdī, attributed to the Prophet: “The servant will not reach the rank of the God-fearing until he leaves what is harmless out of caution against what is harmful.”
